summary: Completed public API regression and focused desktop/mobile UI testing for relationships, case studies, contact, navigation, images, and responsive panels.

integration_issues.flow: Desktop case-study modal scroll-linked engineering stages
integration_issues.issue: The desktop case-study panel is only 24px taller than its viewport (scrollHeight 897, clientHeight 873), so scrolling clamps near zero and active stage remains 1/7. The seven stages and activation work on mobile (active 1->4), but desktop users cannot advance through the stages.

action_items: Make desktop case-study modal content meaningfully scrollable or otherwise map wheel/scroll progress to all seven story stages, then retest desktop activation.
critical_code_review_comments: CaseStudyModal derives stage solely from panel scrollTop, but desktop layout has insufficient overflow for stage progression; the required interaction is therefore viewport-dependent.
seed_data_creation: Created TEST-prefixed contact and status records through the public regression suite; no seeded production data was modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: API health/contact validation/status persistence passed. Relationship panels, official links, close behavior, contact success, capability tabs, image loading, homepage anchors, and 390px overflow passed. Mobile case-study stage activation passed; desktop activation is blocked by only 24px of modal overflow.
rca of the issue: CaseStudyModal listens to case-study-panel scrollTop and divides it by 95, but the desktop two-column panel is nearly shorter than its max-height. The browser clamps scrollTop to roughly 24px, leaving Math.floor(scrollTop / 95) at 0. Increase desktop content height/scroll affordance or implement explicit progress mapping independent of natural overflow.
